input: # An aggregate option value, `option (f) = { a: 1 };`, is the text between
# its braces as protoc 36 records it in `aggregate_value`: every token,
# space and newline as written, with each comment replaced by the newlines
# and spaces that keep the next token on its line and column
# was checked against protoc 36.2's own parser and agrees with it, except
# the one block that says otherwise. ts/src/aggregate.ts has the rule in
# whitespace and newlines between the braces are kept as written, tabs included
# a comment within one line becomes spaces of its width, wherever the option sits
# width is counted in protoc columns: a tab moves to the next multiple of 8, so the same comment is wider or narrower by where it sits
# ... and every byte of UTF-8 is a column, ahead of the brace too
# a comment that ends on a later line becomes its newlines, then spaces up to the column where it ends; a line comment ends after its newline
# comments with nothing between them are one gap
# protoc stops at the closing brace before padding for it, so a comment directly ahead of it leaves nothing, a line comment's newline included
# CRLF: a carriage return is whitespace, and inside a comment it goes with the comment
# comment markers inside a string are text, and adjacent strings are kept apart as written
# braces inside a comment do not count, and nested braces are part of the text
# `/*/` does not close a comment, and `/**/` does
# `#` starts no comment in .proto: protoc keeps it and the rest of its line, for text format to read later (the tabnas lexer skips it, but the text is read from the source)
# a repeated field's values as a list, of scalars or messages, the colon optional before messages (text format's short repeated form)
# a message in angle brackets, `<` and `>`, the colon optional, nested and mixed with braces

# NOT protoc's parser's answer: it takes any run of tokens between balanced braces. Text format refuses these when protoc reads the option (the protoc binary reports it), and so does this package: a trailing or leading comma in a list, a list without commas, a list in a list, an unclosed list or angle bracket, an empty or unclosed name, a name with a leading dot

# protoc's parser refuses these: a list or angle brackets as an option's whole value, braces that do not balance, and a bracketed name its tokenizer cannot read: a number that runs into a letter, a `_` or a second decimal point, a malformed octal or hex number or exponent, a decimal point and a digit directly behind an identifier
